rules.title: Page file (virtual memory)
rules.summary: Virtual memory file; resize it in Performance Options, never delete it
rules.whatItIs: The page file extends RAM: Windows moves rarely used memory pages here, and it is used to write crash dumps.
rules.whyBig: Windows sizes it automatically from installed RAM, recent memory use and crash dump settings, often several GB to tens of GB on PCs with a lot of RAM.
rules.ifDeleted: It is locked while Windows runs. Turning it off entirely can make programs fail with out-of-memory errors and prevents crash dumps.
rules.saferAlternative: System Properties > Advanced > Performance Settings > Advanced > Virtual memory: set a smaller custom size or move it to another drive, then restart.

rules.title: Hibernation file
rules.summary: Saved memory for hibernate and Fast Startup; shrink or turn off with powercfg
rules.whatItIs: Holds the contents of memory when the PC hibernates, and the system session saved by Fast Startup at shutdown.
rules.whyBig: A full hibernation file is reserved at about 40% of installed RAM by default, so a PC with 32 GB of RAM has a file of roughly 13 GB.
rules.ifDeleted: It is locked while Windows runs. Removing it by other means breaks hibernation and Fast Startup.
rules.saferAlternative: 'powercfg /hibernate off' removes the file but also turns off hibernation and Fast Startup. 'powercfg /h /type reduced' keeps Fast Startup with a smaller file (about 20% of RAM).

rules.title: Swap file for Store apps
rules.summary: Swap file for suspended Store apps; managed together with the page file
rules.whatItIs: Windows uses it to swap whole suspended Microsoft Store (packaged) apps out of memory.
rules.ifDeleted: It is locked while Windows runs, and disappears only when the page file on that drive is turned off.

rules.title: Crash dump stack log (in use)
rules.summary: Tiny log of the crash dump driver; locked while Windows runs
rules.whatItIs: Created at every boot by the crash dump components so they can log problems while writing a crash dump.
rules.ifDeleted: It is in use while Windows runs and recreated at each boot; there is nothing to gain.

rules.title: Crash dump stack log
rules.summary: Crash dump stack log from an earlier boot; tiny and safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: A log left by the crash dump components from a previous boot.

rules.title: Windows Boot Manager
rules.summary: Windows Boot Manager; the PC cannot start Windows without it
rules.whatItIs: The Windows Boot Manager program loaded by the firmware on BIOS-style boot partitions. UEFI PCs use bootmgfw.efi on the EFI partition instead, and Windows keeps master copies under Windows\Boot.
rules.ifDeleted: The PC can no longer boot Windows from this drive.

rules.title: Boot helper file (BOOTNXT)
rules.summary: Small boot file that sits next to bootmgr
rules.whatItIs: A tiny file used by the Windows boot process on BIOS-style system partitions.
rules.ifDeleted: Booting may fail on PCs that use it.

rules.title: Memory dump
rules.summary: Crash or memory dump for debugging; safe to delete unless you need to report a crash
rules.whatItIs: A snapshot of a process's or of the system's memory, written when something crashed or when a dump was requested for debugging.
rules.whyBig: A dump contains the memory of the crashed process or of the whole system, from a few MB to many GB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the crash it describes can no longer be analysed.
rules.saferAlternative: Keep it only if you plan to send it to a developer or support.

rules.title: Heap dump (Windows Error Reporting)
rules.summary: Crash dump with heap memory, written by Windows Error Reporting
rules.whatItIs: A crash dump that includes the crashed process's heap, collected by Windows Error Reporting for a crash report.
rules.whyBig: Heap dumps contain much of the process's memory, often hundreds of MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the report can no longer be analysed.

rules.title: Minidump
rules.summary: Small crash dump; safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: A small crash dump written by Windows Error Reporting or an application's crash handler.
rules.whyBig: Usually a few MB; repeated crashes add up.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; the crash can no longer be analysed.

rules.title: Event trace log
rules.summary: Diagnostic trace from Windows or an app; old traces are safe to delete
rules.whatItIs: An Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) log written by Windows components, drivers or tools such as Windows Performance Recorder.
rules.whyBig: Some traces run continuously and rotate; performance recordings can be hundreds of MB.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; traces that are being written are locked. Keep traces you recorded on purpose for analysis.

rules.title: Windows event log
rules.summary: Event Viewer log; clear it or cap its size in Event Viewer
rules.whatItIs: A Windows event log file as shown in Event Viewer.
rules.whyBig: Each log grows until its configured maximum size; logs set to archive instead of overwrite keep growing.
rules.ifDeleted: Active logs are locked while the Event Log service runs; deleting closed or exported logs only loses their history.
rules.saferAlternative: In Event Viewer, right-click the log > Properties to lower its maximum size, or choose Clear Log.

rules.title: User registry hive
rules.summary: Your personal registry (settings of Windows and apps) and its logs
rules.whatItIs: NTUSER.DAT is the registry hive of one user profile; the .LOG, .blf and .regtrans-ms files next to it are its transaction logs.
rules.whyBig: Usually a few MB to a few hundred MB; it grows with the settings that apps write.
rules.ifDeleted: The profile can no longer sign in properly; Windows signs you in with a temporary profile.

rules.title: User registry hive (classes)
rules.summary: Per-user registry part for file associations and app registrations
rules.whatItIs: UsrClass.dat holds the per-user part of the registry for file associations, COM registrations and Store app data, with its log files.
rules.whyBig: Usually tens of MB; it can grow with many Store apps.
rules.ifDeleted: Start, Store apps and file associations break for this profile.

rules.title: Explorer thumbnail cache
rules.summary: Thumbnail previews File Explorer has cached; rebuilt automatically
rules.whatItIs: Database of thumbnail images that File Explorer shows for pictures, videos and documents.
rules.whyBig: It grows with every folder of pictures and videos you browse in thumbnail view, and old entries are not always removed.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; thumbnails are regenerated when folders are opened again. Files in use by Explorer are locked.
rules.saferAlternative: Storage settings > Temporary files > Thumbnails clears it cleanly.

rules.title: Explorer icon cache
rules.summary: Cached icons used by File Explorer; rebuilt automatically
rules.whatItIs: Database of icons extracted from programs and file types, so Explorer does not have to load them again.
rules.ifDeleted: Nothing breaks; icons are rebuilt, and files in use by Explorer are locked.
